brief.topic: A Small Cut Changes the Song

s01: Two wind chimes share the same material and thickness.
One is shorter, and its bending note is higher.
Here is a simple tone for each chime.
These tubes bend sideways when struck.
The ends move, while two places along each tube barely move.
We show that bending slowly so its shape is visible.
For this ideal beam model, frequency follows one divided by length squared.
Make the length about seventy-one percent as large, and the frequency doubles.
The shorter tube is not half as long.
Here the lengths differ by a factor of the square root of two.
Their modeled notes are two hundred and twenty, and four hundred and forty hertz.
These pure tones represent the lowest bending mode.
A real chime adds other modes and a changing decay.
The rule assumes slender tubes with the same material and cross-section.
A small change in length can make a larger change in the sound.

scenes.narration:
Two wind chimes share the same material and thickness. One is shorter, and its bending note is higher. Here is a simple tone for each chime.

These tubes bend sideways when struck. The ends move, while two places along each tube barely move. We show that bending slowly so its shape is visible.

For this ideal beam model, frequency follows one divided by length squared. Make the length about seventy-one percent as large, and the frequency doubles. The shorter tube is not half as long.

Here the lengths differ by a factor of the square root of two. Their modeled notes are two hundred and twenty, and four hundred and forty hertz. Hear that comparison again.

These pure tones represent the lowest bending mode. A real chime adds other modes and a changing decay. The rule assumes slender tubes with the same material and cross-section. A small change in length can make a larger change in the sound.
